departures.decided: before any accepted timing run, with positive controls of both verdicts (runs/control, not published)
departures.done: Before a run, at least 70 percent CPU idle averaged over 10 s, read with iostat inside the slots immediately before timing (waiting up to 240 s); during a run, idle sampled every 2 s and the run discarded when its mean fell below 50 percent; the one-minute load still recorded before and after every run; three attempts.
departures.registered: the one-minute load is read inside the slot before timing starts and again after; a run whose load before exceeds 8 is discarded and retried, three attempts at most, after which the point is recorded as not measured with its loads
departures.why: On this shared machine the one-minute load stayed between 13.9 and 16.5 while the CPU was 77 to 88 percent idle: the load counts thousands of threads other processes hold, none of which a measurement can pause, so no run could ever have passed the registered rule. Idle measures the CPU a run competes for directly.

departures.done: Each repeat is four sessions from the arrival point, each with its own open and arrival reference: the controls (40 and 80 m), 1 km, 4 km and 8 km. The 8 km session is the whole 0 to 8 km sprint for frame work.
departures.registered: one continuous walk per repeat, stopping at each mark
departures.what: distance walks split into one mark per page session
departures.why: The headless measuring browser stopped answering during the third sprint of a session after two place-and-take-back cycles, in the first registered attempt and in five dry runs after it: the page kept running while the browser process ran at 80 to 92 percent CPU and no DevTools client could connect. Image transfer, pointer lock, the on-device model service and storage writes were each excluded; the cause was not identified. It is the measuring browser, not the product.

departures.why: Dry walks to 40 and 80 m showed the registered silhouette shifting by more than a pixel where float32 spacing is below a hundredth of a millimetre.

how_to_rerun: Restore the scripts: copy scripts/*.txt to their names without .txt and reverse the stated substitutions.
Start an isolated runtime at the measured commit (the acceptance launcher, one slot, --no-derivative-worker for the estimates runtime), build the app with vite build and serve it with preview.py up.
Objects: python3 series.py --layout spread, then --layout clustered in a fresh runtime (each count runs step.py through slot.py --gpu).
Debug against release: python3 slot.py --gpu -- python3 compare.py --label cmp-clustered-200 --objects 200, with the development server up.
Distance: python3 distance.py --repeats 3 in a world with no object.
Estimates: python3 rooms.py, then python3 estimates_series.py --counts 1,4,16,32 (depth runs through slot.py --gpu -- python3 worker.py run --once).

Inhabitants: python3 slot.py -- .venv/bin/python society_scale.py population --out runs/society/population.json --populations 32,128,512,2048 --ticks 60, then society_scale.py history --out runs/society/history.json --checkpoints 1,60,240,1440.
Analysis: .venv/bin/python shading.py; python3 pointcounts.py DATA_DIR; python3 outcome.py summary; python3 publish.py; .venv/bin/python write_outcome.py.

incidents.detail: An undo click fell below the objects panel's fold, so the world was left holding 11 objects and reload, walking and looking measured 11. The run was set aside, the stray object taken back through the product's undo route, the driver changed to scroll a target into view and to check the world's count through the API, and the point measured again.

incidents.detail: The instrument counted only nodes attached one at a time, and a placed estimate is built inside its parent before the parent joins the scene, so open and reload never saw the world complete. The instrument now counts named nodes across every attached subtree; the point was measured again.

answer: The first limit a person meets is opening a world that holds photo estimates. Opening stays within 2 s up to 16 placed estimates (1,103.6 ms) and exceeds it at 32 (2,028.6 ms, all five warm opens over); it grows by about 57.8 ms an estimate. At the registered two minutes an estimate, that is between 32 and 64 minutes of placing estimates (MEASURED knee, ASSUMED rate).

The second is the objects panel's acknowledgement of a placement or a take-back: 121.7 ms at 200 spread objects and 829.3 ms at 1000 (1,469.0 ms clustered), against 250 ms. At the registered thirty seconds a placement, that is between 100 and 500 minutes of placing objects (MEASURED knee, ASSUMED rate).

Frame work never approaches its budget: the largest 95th percentile at any object point is 2.0 ms against 16.7 ms, at 1000 objects, and every sprint to 8 km keeps it within 0.7 ms, with a few single long frames in some legs (see the distance series). Every reload at every count showed the saved world exactly (MEASURED).

Two limits no budget measures arrive much sooner, and were found answering a registered open question: the sky is no longer drawn at 1 km (MEASURED), past about 540 m from where the world opened by the code (INFERRED, about 23 s of sprinting), and at 4 km objects' lit faces carry diagonal bands they do not have at 1 km (MEASURED).

The society's replay exceeds 2 s between 1 and 60 ticks of history at 128 inhabitants (2,291.2 ms at 60), and a tick at 512 inhabitants exceeds 250 ms (513.1 ms); no product path reaches either at this commit.
The combined world, 200 spread objects and 16 estimates at once, passes every budget: first frame 1,431.6 ms, complete world 1,602.2 ms.

assumed_rates.society: playback at speed 1, one tick per second

first_limits.limit: Opening a saved world that holds photo estimates takes longer than the 2 s budget.
first_limits.register: MEASURED knee; INFERRED crossing (straight line between the medians at 16 and 32)
first_limits.reproduction: Place 32 photo estimates into one saved world on the endless ground through the product (intake, the review granting the depth right, the depth worker, then Place for each), reload the page and time the first drawn frame from the operator token's submit; every one of five warm opens took over 2 s.
first_limits.why_it_grows: READ by the pre-registration in the code (loadAuthoredPointMaps runs before the renderer mounts) and consistent with what was MEASURED: every placed estimate is fetched and hashed before the renderer mounts, so the first drawn frame waits for all of them and equals the complete world at every count (submit to first frame 1,968.4 ms of the 2,028.6 ms at 32). The point maps are 3,877,264 to 3,915,944 bytes each.

first_limits.limit: The objects panel's report that a placement or its take-back has landed arrives later than the 250 ms budget.
first_limits.register: MEASURED knee; INFERRED crossing (the chord between 200 and 1000; the acknowledgement steepens with count, so if it keeps doing so the true crossing is at or after the chord's)
first_limits.reproduction: Build a saved world of 1000 objects through the product's composition routes, open it, place one object with Place before me and Confirm, and time the panel's settled report; then take it back. All five placements and five take-backs took over 250 ms in both layouts.
first_limits.spread_between_runs: At clustered 1000 the five acknowledgements ranged from 773.1 ms to 1,734.7 ms and fell over the last four; every one is over the budget, so the verdict does not depend on the spread. Its cause is not established.
first_limits.why_it_grows: INFERRED from MEASURED times: the last object becomes resident again only just before the report settles (776.5 ms of 829.3 ms at spread 1000), while the server's apply takes 79.0 ms: the time is the page redrawing every object after each change, the mechanism the pre-registration read in the code (settle awaits redrawAll).

limits_added_after_registration.defect: Probable defect: the endless ground has no edge but the sky does. Not fixed here.
limits_added_after_registration.inferred: The sky is lost past about 540 m from the opening point: 23.1 s of sprinting or 60.0 s of walking. Where between 80 m and 1 km it happens was not measured.
limits_added_after_registration.limit: The sky stops being drawn once the camera is farther than the sky sphere's radius from where the world opened.
limits_added_after_registration.measured: In all nine sessions at 1, 4 and 8 km the sky band of the capture is the camera's flat clear colour (one distinct colour in the 286 rows at x 720); at the arrival point it holds 30 colours and at 40 and 80 m it is still a gradient.
limits_added_after_registration.read: web/packages/atlas-react/src/playcanvas/composed-world.ts places the sky, a unit sphere scaled to 540 m, at the opening frame (setPosition(frame.x, 0, frame.z), setLocalScale(540, 540, 540)) and nothing moves it afterwards; the camera's far clip outside a city is 1,200 m (atlas-binding.ts).
limits_added_after_registration.reproduction: Open any saved world on the endless ground, hold W and Shift for 30 s, and look ahead: the sky above the horizon is one flat colour.
limits_added_after_registration.why_not_a_knee: No budget measures the sky; it answers a registered open question and was added after registration.

limits_added_after_registration.inferred: Cause not established. Consistent with shadow-map or depth precision at large world coordinates, since the cube's own silhouette stays within about a pixel.
limits_added_after_registration.limit: Lit faces of objects carry diagonal bands at 4 and 8 km that they do not have at 1 km.
limits_added_after_registration.measured: The reference cube's lit face (11,328 pixels) differs from its own arrival capture by more than 8 levels in 7,065, 6,982, 6,859 pixels at 4 km and 7,021, 7,292, 7,242 at 8 km (three repeats), and in none at 40 m, 80 m or 1 km.
limits_added_after_registration.reproduction: Sprint 4 km from the arrival point, place a marker cube with Place before me and look at its lit face at the capture pose.
limits_added_after_registration.why_not_a_knee: No budget measures shading; added after registration.

limits_no_product_path_reaches.limit: Replaying a society's history takes longer than the 2 s budget after less than a minute of playback.
limits_no_product_path_reaches.minutes_of_ordinary_use: between 1 s and 1 minute of playback at speed 1 (one tick a second)
limits_no_product_path_reaches.register: MEASURED knee; INFERRED crossing (chord between 1 and 60 ticks); READ callers
limits_no_product_path_reaches.why_it_follows: Replay is served only by GET /world/versions/{id}/society/replay (exulanica/api/routes/society.py); no web client code and no server process calls it at the measured commit, and this runtime's readiness report says no saved world holds inhabitants without a registration file. The ranking rule orders limits no product path reaches after those a person meets.

limits_no_product_path_reaches.limit: A society tick at 512 inhabitants takes longer than the 250 ms budget.
limits_no_product_path_reaches.why_it_follows: 512 inhabitants were made by overriding the creation constant inside the measuring process; the engine and the database accept 512 but no product path creates it at the measured commit (the product makes 128).

registered_failure_present_at_the_arriva.statistic_sensitivity: The registration names no statistic across repeats for this metric; the median is used, as for every other repeated metric. Under the smallest repeat the knee is also between 1 and 4 km; under the largest it would fall before 1 km, since one 1 km repeat exceeds a pixel.
registered_failure_present_at_the_arriva.why_it_is_not_ranked_as_a_scale_limit: The registered silhouette is the capture with the reference minus the capture without it, so it includes the cube's soft shadow and the line where its base meets the ground. It exceeds a pixel at the 40 and 80 m controls as well, where float32 spacing is below a hundredth of a millimetre, so the change it measures is present within 80 m of the arrival point and is not caused by distance. The object-only silhouette (shadow casting off for one frame, added before any registered walk) moves by at most about two pixels at every mark, with no trend.

outcome.rule: limits a person meets through the product are ranked by the minutes of ordinary use before they appear; limits no product path reaches at this commit follow them

predecessor_record.why: The pre-registration: budgets, series, statistics, knee rule, stop rules and ranking rule, written before the first timing run and unchanged since. Every verdict here is judged against it, and every departure from it is listed under departures.

predictions.evidence: It is the first budget to fail within the object series, in both layouts, between 200 and 1000. It is not linear from zero: flat to 10 objects (32.4 ms at 0, 32.9 ms at 10), then 0.4 ms more an object from 50 to 200 and 0.9 ms from 200 to 1000 in the spread layout (0.6 ms and 1.7 ms clustered). The time to the last object resident tracks the acknowledgement at every count, as the redraw mechanism predicts.
predictions.prediction: Placement and undo acknowledgement grow linearly with placed objects: settle awaits redrawAll, which clears every resident object and fetches, hashes, decodes and attaches each one again, one at a time (web/packages/app/src/composition/objects.ts settle, redrawAll, drawEvery; web/packages/atlas-react/src/playcanvas/scene-objects.ts place). Predicted to be the first budget to fail, in both layouts.

predictions.evidence: First frame, spread: 120.8 ms at 0, 132.5 ms at 200, 211.0 ms at 1000; clustered 135.8 ms, 154.6 ms, 257.3 ms. Estimates: 238.6 ms at 1 to 2,028.6 ms at 32, and the first frame equals the complete world at every estimate count.
predictions.prediction: Open to first drawn frame does not grow with objects, which are drawn after the renderer mounts (main.ts calls objects.begin after mountRenderer), and does grow with placed estimates, which are fetched and hashed before it mounts (loadAuthoredPointMaps).
predictions.verdict: held for estimates; for objects held to 200 and not at 1000

predictions.evidence: Complete world, spread: 120.8 ms at 0, 170.9 ms at 10, 214.3 ms at 50, 279.8 ms at 200, 628.3 ms at 1000; clustered: 135.8 ms at 0, 160.5 ms at 10, 198.2 ms at 50, 283.0 ms at 200, 935.7 ms at 1000.
predictions.prediction: Open to complete world grows linearly with objects, for the reason in the first prediction.

predictions.prediction: The server's apply grows with objects: every edit digests every object (object_repository._append_edit, delta_sha256) and answers with every object and every edit.

predictions.evidence: Walking p95, spread 0.5 ms at 0 and 1.6 ms at 1000; clustered 0.3 ms and 1.9 ms. Draw calls at p50: spread 450, clustered 2003 at 1000.
predictions.prediction: Frame work while walking grows with objects in view, one entity and draw per object with no instancing, faster clustered than spread.

record.subject: How large a saved world grows through the product's own routes before opening, reloading, placing and taking back, walking or looking around stops meeting its registered budget, measured on one machine at one commit.

tree.how: slot.py refused to start any slot unless HEAD was the measured commit and git diff --quiet HEAD and git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all were clean for exulanica, web/packages, migrations, pyproject.toml and web/package.json. Every browser run file carries the tree it ran on (head, diff bytes 0); the society files carry measured_commit.
tree.measurement_code: outside the product paths, published under scripts/ beside this record
tree.rule: Every figure names the commit it ran on. Before each run the product paths (exulanica/, web/packages/, migrations) are checked unchanged from that commit with git diff --quiet and git status. Measurement drivers live outside the product paths.
